description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of monolingual and multilingual datasets over the years from 2012 to 2022. The horizontal axis represents the years, labeled in one-year increments from 2012 to 2022, while the vertical axis represents the number of datasets on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^2. Each year is associated with a pair of bars, with the blue bar representing monolingual datasets (labeled as '1') and the orange bar representing multilingual datasets (labeled as '2+'). The height of the bars corresponds to the number of datasets, with the blue bars consistently being taller than or equal to the orange bars. The number of monolingual datasets starts at a low value in 2012, around 2, and increases steadily to a peak of around 120 in 2021, with a slight decrease in 2022 to around 40 (light blue shading). Multilingual datasets first appear in 2017 with a value of around 6, and increase to a maximum of around 40 in 2020, before decreasing to around 2 in 2022. The bars are grouped by year, with the blue bar always preceding the orange bar. Notably, the 2022 bars are shaded lighter than the preceding bars.
